network.question: A packet capture shows a host sending an Ethernet frame to the MAC of its default gateway while the IP destination is a remote web server. Which explanation BEST fits the capture?
options: The host is incorrectly addressing the web server to the gateway MAC
The host uses the next-hop MAC for the local Ethernet frame while preserving the remote destination IP
The gateway is performing an ARP broadcast for the remote web server
The web server and gateway must be on the same VLAN
network.explanation: For off-subnet destinations the Ethernet destination MAC is the local next hop; the IP destination remains the remote server. It does not imply an incorrect address, a remote ARP query, or shared VLAN membership.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: An application uses one public HTTPS endpoint but must route /payments and /reports requests to different healthy backend pools. Which solution BEST satisfies both requirements?
options: A Layer 4 TCP load balancer using only destination port
An authoritative DNS server using weighted records
A Layer 7 HTTPS load balancer using URL paths and health checks
An HTTP reverse proxy routing every request to the same backend
network.explanation: The application must inspect the request path and route to separate healthy backend pools, so a Layer 7 HTTPS load balancer is required. Layer 4 cannot route by URL, weighted DNS cannot inspect paths, and a fixed reverse proxy does not distribute requests across healthy pools.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A cloud migration requires the organization to manage the guest operating system but not the underlying hypervisor hardware. Which service model BEST matches?
network.explanation: IaaS leaves OS and application management with the customer while the provider runs physical compute. PaaS abstracts the guest OS; SaaS supplies applications; DaaS is more specialized.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A software-defined network controller decides which routes and policies should be installed on switches. The switches then forward packets accordingly. Which pair of functions is described?
options: Data plane deciding policy; control plane transmitting packets
Management plane forwarding data; physical plane setting routes
Application plane handling MAC learning; control plane forwarding user traffic
Control plane making decisions; data plane forwarding traffic
network.explanation: The control plane determines routes and policies, and the data plane implements forwarding. The other alternatives reverse those responsibilities or describe unrelated planes.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A remote office reports low throughput only when an encrypted site-to-site tunnel is active. ICMP packets of 1,400 bytes with DF set succeed, but 1,470-byte DF packets fail. Which setting should be investigated FIRST?
options: An IPsec SA lifetime that is too short
MTU or TCP MSS across the encrypted VPN path
A DNS negative-caching TTL that is too high
network.explanation: Encrypted VPN encapsulation reduces the usable payload MTU; failure only for larger DF packets points to path MTU/MSS. IKE rekey or SA lifetime issues would not predictably affect packets at one size threshold, and DNS TTL does not cause a size-specific ICMP failure.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A branch application uses a CDN. The site responds quickly for users near an edge location even when the origin is on another continent. What BEST accounts for the improvement?
options: Caching requested content at CDN edge locations
Changing authoritative DNS to a longer TTL without caching
Sending all requests through a single origin load balancer
Using only origin-server compression with no edge storage
network.explanation: CDN edge caching serves a nearby copy and avoids repeated long-distance origin round trips. DNS TTL alone cannot deliver uncached content, an origin load balancer remains far away, and compression does not eliminate distance or origin fetches.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A team must place 54 workstations, 12 printers, and 5 servers in separate IPv4 subnets within 10.60.8.0/24. Which subnet size combination wastes the fewest addresses while accommodating each group?
network.explanation: A /26 provides 62 hosts for 54, /28 provides 14 for 12, and /29 provides 6 for 5. /27 cannot host 54; /29 is too small for 12; larger prefixes waste more addresses.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: An engineer assigns a host 172.16.18.94/27 with gateway 172.16.18.65. The host cannot reach the gateway. What BEST describes the problem?
options: The default gateway is on another /27 subnet
The gateway is the network address for this /27 subnet
The host IP is the broadcast address
Both addresses are valid hosts on the same /27 subnet
network.explanation: A /27 block spans .64–.95, with .65–.94 usable. Both .94 and .65 are valid, so the failure must have another cause; the stated addresses are not the error.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A subnet starts at 192.168.40.96/27. Which address can be assigned to an endpoint that requires a usable unicast host address?
network.explanation: The /27 covers .96–.127: .96 is network and .127 broadcast; .126 is the last usable. .95 belongs to the preceding block.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: An AWS VPC is 10.24.0.0/20. Which subnet is fully inside it and does not overlap the separate subnet 10.24.0.0/22?
network.explanation: The /20 covers 10.24.0.0–10.24.15.255; 10.24.4.0/22 covers .4–.7 and does not overlap .0–.3. The /21 overlaps and .16 is outside the /20.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A workstation has IP 10.10.4.190 and mask 255.255.255.192. Its default gateway is 10.10.4.129. Which result should you expect?
options: The workstation is on 10.10.4.192/26 and cannot reach the gateway
The workstation and gateway are both in 10.10.4.128/26
The workstation is a broadcast address
The gateway is the broadcast address
network.explanation: The /26 block 10.10.4.128–191 contains .129 and .190 as usable hosts. Neither is a network or broadcast address.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A technician must summarize the contiguous routes 10.22.8.0/24 through 10.22.11.0/24 into one route. Which CIDR prefix is the smallest exact summary?
network.explanation: Four aligned /24 networks from third octet 8 through 11 fit exactly into 10.22.8.0/22. /23 covers only two; /21 and /20 include extra networks.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: An AP is managed untagged in VLAN 10 and broadcasts employee SSID VLAN 20 and guest SSID VLAN 30. Which switch-port configuration BEST supports this design?
options: Native VLAN 30 and tagged VLAN 10 only
Native VLAN 20 and block all tagged VLANs
network.explanation: Management remains untagged in VLAN 10; both SSIDs must traverse the uplink tagged. Single access or incomplete trunk configurations drop at least one network.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: Two switches are connected with 802.1Q. VLAN 30 works locally on both switches, but devices in VLAN 30 cannot talk across the uplink. VLAN 10 works across it. What should be checked FIRST?
options: An STP-blocked port on the uplink that passes VLAN 10
An inconsistent native VLAN that affects only untagged frames
VLAN 30 missing from the allowed tagged VLAN list on either end
An incorrect VLAN 30 default gateway on both switches
network.explanation: The uplink carries VLAN 10 successfully, but VLAN 30 fails only across the link; missing tagged VLAN permission is the strongest explanation.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A newly installed redundant switch link causes a broadcast storm and unstable MAC address tables. Which technology would normally prevent this Layer 2 loop?
options: LACP link bundling without loop protection
Storm control rate limiting without path blocking
network.explanation: STP prevents Layer 2 loops by blocking redundant forwarding paths. LACP bundles links but needs correctly managed topology; storm control limits traffic rates without fixing the loop; port security limits MAC learning rather than topology.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: An administrator enables port security with a maximum of one learned MAC address. An IP phone with a PC connected through its downstream port loses connectivity after the PC sends traffic. What is the MOST likely reason?
options: A voice VLAN mismatch at the uplink
A missing QoS trust boundary for the phone
A DHCP scope option for the phone subnet is wrong
The port learns two endpoint MAC addresses and violates the limit
network.explanation: A phone with a downstream PC can present two MAC addresses, exceeding a one-MAC security limit. A voice VLAN mismatch could affect phone service but not explain the stated violation trigger; QoS and DHCP options do not increase the learned-MAC allowance.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A workstation in VLAN 40 can reach other devices in VLAN 40 but not servers in VLAN 50. Routing is configured, but a firewall rule denies VLAN 40 to VLAN 50. Which change is MOST appropriate?
options: Change the VLAN 50 port to a tagged trunk
Allow only the necessary VLAN 40-to-server traffic through the firewall
Permit all traffic between VLANs 40 and 50
Disable inter-VLAN ACLs for the entire site
network.explanation: The scenario explicitly identifies a VLAN 40→50 firewall deny rule. Narrowly permitting required application traffic solves the need while retaining segmentation. Changing switch trunking, allowing all traffic, or turning off the full ACL policy is overly broad or misses the cause.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: An engineer notices frequent topology changes after connecting a consumer switch to an enterprise switch access port. Which feature BEST reduces the risk of a rogue switch becoming the STP root?
options: Root Guard on every workstation-facing port
Storm Control configured only for multicast
BPDU Guard on designated edge/access ports
DHCP Snooping with all downstream ports trusted
network.explanation: An edge port receiving unexpected BPDUs should be guarded against rogue switching connections: BPDU Guard is the appropriate control. Root Guard addresses root selection; Storm Control limits broadcasts; DHCP snooping does not detect BPDUs.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A router has 10.2.0.0/16 via Router A, 10.2.8.0/21 via Router B, and 10.2.10.0/24 via Router C. Which next hop is selected for 10.2.10.50?
network.explanation: Longest-prefix match selects the most specific matching route: /24 via Router C beats /21 and /16.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: Two routers advertise the same destination prefix using OSPF. One has total cost 30; the other has cost 10. Assuming both routes are valid, which path is preferred?
options: Both must be load-balanced regardless of cost
Whichever route has the highest hop count
network.explanation: OSPF prefers the lowest accumulated cost. Equal-cost paths may be load-balanced, but unequal costs do not require that.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: Clients in VLAN 20 can reach an internal server by IP but not any public IP address. The gateway WAN is online and has a public address. Which missing configuration is a LIKELY cause?
options: An outbound route that is used only by VLAN 10
An outbound SNAT/PAT rule covering VLAN 20
A DNS forwarder that answers only internal zones
An ARP entry for VLAN 20 gateway on the switch
network.explanation: Without appropriate source NAT, private clients may not have usable return connectivity to the public internet. DNS is not involved when testing public IP directly.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A company wants both branch offices to reach an internal subnet through encrypted tunnels, but routing should automatically converge when a tunnel fails. Which design BEST addresses the routing requirement?
options: Static routes that never change after a failed tunnel
Static routes with no route-health tracking
A single default route through the primary VPN
Dynamic routing across redundant VPN paths
network.explanation: Dynamic routing across the redundant VPNs can converge when one path fails. Unmonitored static routes, a single default tunnel, and static routes without health checks cannot automatically adapt to a tunnel outage.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: The route 0.0.0.0/0 exists on a firewall, but the VLAN 30 client has no default gateway configured. What will the client do with a destination outside its subnet?
options: Use the firewall route automatically without sending to a gateway
Broadcast the packet directly to every internet router
Fail to send off-subnet traffic because it has no next hop
Use DNS as the default gateway
network.explanation: A route on the firewall does not replace the client-side default gateway. The client cannot determine its next hop for off-subnet traffic.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A router performs source NAT for 10.1.0.0/16. A new 10.2.0.0/16 VLAN is added, and internal routing works but internet access fails. Which change should be tested FIRST?
options: Include 10.2.0.0/16 in the appropriate outbound NAT policy
Increase NAT timeout values for 10.1.0.0/16 only
Enable destination NAT toward the internal management network
network.explanation: The NAT policy covers only the original private range, making missing source NAT a strong candidate; routing already works internally.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A site has two DHCP servers with identical scopes on the same broadcast domain. Clients intermittently receive duplicate addresses. Which remediation BEST preserves DHCP redundancy?
options: Use shorter leases on both identical scopes
Deploy coordinated DHCP failover or nonoverlapping scope allocations
Configure both DHCP servers with the same reservation table only
network.explanation: Coordinated failover or carefully nonoverlapping scopes avoids conflicting address allocation. Identical independent pools can create collisions even with shorter leases or matching reservations.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A newly configured VLAN 70 has a routed interface and the gateway answers pings. Clients still obtain 169.254.x.x addresses. The DHCP server is on a different subnet. What should you inspect FIRST?
options: Expand the VLAN 70 DHCP scope before testing relay
DHCP relay/helper address on the VLAN 70 interface
Enable DHCP snooping trust on all client ports
Add an IP helper on the DHCP server’s local interface only
network.explanation: DHCP clients in VLAN 70 must reach the off-subnet DHCP server through a helper/relay. Expanding a scope or trusting all edge ports will not forward broadcasts, and a relay on the DHCP server interface does not replace a helper for the client VLAN.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: Network monitoring shows interfaces with increasing CRC errors but no major changes in link utilization. What is the BEST initial investigation?
options: A mismatched full-duplex setting or failing copper pair
An OSPF cost change after convergence
Physical cable, termination and transceiver health
network.explanation: Increasing CRC errors indicate frame corruption or duplex/physical problems. Check the cable, transceiver and link negotiation before investigating application-layer causes.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A company wants to restore customer services within 90 minutes and tolerate no more than 15 minutes of lost data after a disaster. Which targets are correct?
network.explanation: RTO limits service restoration time; RPO limits recoverable data loss measured in time. The other responses reverse or substitute unrelated metrics.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A network manager needs detailed time-series information about interface utilization across many switches using centrally polled counters. Which technology is MOST appropriate?
options: Syslog event aggregation without traffic counters
Flow logs sampled only for application sessions
SNMP polling of interface octet counters over time
network.explanation: SNMP polling collects interface octet counters repeatedly to calculate utilization over time. Flow logs describe sessions and traffic patterns; syslog alone records events; NTP offsets measure clock drift rather than bandwidth.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: Two monitoring systems report conflicting timestamps after an outage. What service should be fixed before correlating events?
options: NTP time synchronization of monitoring sources
Reordering the SIEM correlation rules only
Changing each log timezone label without fixing device clocks
network.explanation: NTP synchronization fixes the underlying time inconsistency across systems. SIEM normalization can adjust formats but not inherently correct wrong device clocks. Reordering correlation rules or changing timezone labels leaves clock offsets.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A network firewall must allow administrators to use encrypted terminal sessions to Linux servers but block unencrypted Telnet. Which change BEST satisfies the requirement?
options: Allow UDP 22 only and deny TCP 23
network.explanation: SSH normally uses TCP 22 and Telnet TCP 23. RDP uses 3389; SSH is not normally a UDP-only service.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A mail client must retrieve messages securely using IMAP with TLS on its standard dedicated port. What should the firewall allow?
network.explanation: IMAPS uses TCP 993. POP3S uses 995; SMTP submission uses 587; 143 is standard IMAP and may use STARTTLS but is not the dedicated IMAPS port.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A firewall rule should permit DNS queries and zone-transfer traffic to an authoritative DNS server. Which default service ports must be considered?
network.explanation: DNS commonly uses UDP 53 for queries and TCP 53 for zone transfers or larger exchanges. DHCP, LDAP, and SNMP use other ports.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A Windows file server is accessible through RDP but users cannot map SMB network shares. Which port is MOST relevant to check?
network.explanation: Modern SMB file sharing primarily uses TCP 445. RDP can work over 3389 independently; NTP and LDAPS are separate services.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A web application supports HTTP/3 and falls back to HTTPS over HTTP/2 when necessary. Which ports should the edge firewall allow?
network.explanation: HTTP/2 over TLS uses TCP 443; HTTP/3 uses QUIC over UDP 443. Port 80 could be used for redirects but is not required for those two encrypted transports.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A monitoring team can poll SNMP metrics but never receives unsolicited device traps. Which rule is the MOST relevant to check?
options: Inbound UDP 162 at the trap collector
Inbound UDP 161 at the trap collector
Outbound UDP 161 from the monitoring console
Inbound TCP 514 at the monitored switch
network.explanation: SNMP traps are commonly sent to UDP 162 on the management receiver, while polling commonly uses UDP 161.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A switch receives DHCP Offers from an unauthorized workstation and some clients receive the wrong gateway. Which security feature BEST mitigates this without blocking legitimate clients?
options: Enable DHCP snooping with trusted server-facing ports
Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection without DHCP snooping
Configure IP Source Guard only on the attacker workstation
Allow DHCP offers from all access ports
network.explanation: DHCP snooping allows offers from trusted server-facing paths and rejects untrusted edge DHCP replies. Dynamic ARP Inspection validates ARP, IP Source Guard checks source IP bindings, and trusting all access ports would permit rogue servers.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A company needs to enforce certificate-based authentication before endpoints receive ordinary access to switch ports. Which solution BEST fits?
options: MAC Authentication Bypass with a static MAC allowlist
IP Source Guard based on DHCP bindings
Port Security with a maximum of one MAC
network.explanation: 802.1X/EAP-TLS with RADIUS can authenticate device certificates before allowing access. MAC Authentication Bypass and port security trust address identity, and IP Source Guard validates IP/MAC bindings instead of credentials.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A remote employee must access a sensitive management VLAN. Policy requires device identity verification and encryption. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
options: Publicly expose management HTTPS to the internet
Allow access from any IP with only a shared password
Use a secure remote-access VPN with certificate-based device checks
Turn off routing between the employee and management networks
network.explanation: An authenticated encrypted VPN with device identity controls fits the stated access requirement. Public exposure increases risk, and blocking routes prevents access entirely.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A compromised guest laptop is detected trying to reach the server-management VLAN. Which control is the BEST direct containment measure?
options: Increase guest SSID client isolation without controlling routed traffic
Change the guest VLAN DHCP scope to a shorter lease
Block all guest internet egress but allow internal traffic
Deny guest-to-management access with inter-VLAN ACL/firewall policies
network.explanation: Routed guest-to-management access should be denied through an inter-VLAN ACL or firewall rule. Wireless client isolation may not block routed management access; shorter leases do not enforce isolation; blocking internet but allowing internal targets does the opposite of the requirement.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A switch is vulnerable to ARP spoofing. DHCP snooping already builds trusted IP-to-MAC bindings. Which feature BEST uses those bindings to reject forged ARP replies?
options: DHCP snooping alone without ARP validation
Port security limiting the number of MACs
network.explanation: Dynamic ARP Inspection validates ARP claims against trusted bindings and helps block spoofed ARP. DHCP snooping supplies binding information but does not itself inspect every ARP; port security and 802.1X enforce other aspects of admission.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A security administrator wants to restrict access to a switch port based on authenticating people and devices, rather than merely filtering MAC addresses. Which is the BEST choice?
options: MAC Authentication Bypass based on known addresses
DHCP Snooping applied to access ports
Dynamic ARP Inspection based on trusted bindings
network.explanation: 802.1X provides authentication-based admission; MAC and ARP controls do not strongly verify identity.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: An IPv6 host has a global unicast address but cannot discover the local router. Its Neighbor Discovery traffic is filtered. What should be allowed?
options: Enable IPv4 ARP replies on all routed interfaces
Permit ICMPv6 NDP and Router Advertisement messages
Configure DHCPv6 only and drop all Router Advertisements
Allow only ICMPv6 Echo Replies, not NDP
network.explanation: IPv6 uses ICMPv6 for neighbor/router discovery. ARP is IPv4, and DHCPv4 ports are not used for this IPv6 function.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A /64 IPv6 LAN uses SLAAC. An engineer shortens it to /80 without changing host configuration. What risk is MOST relevant?
options: IPv6 default-router advertisements are no longer required
Every IPv6 subnet must use NAT66 after the change
IPv6 TCP cannot operate outside a /64
Traditional SLAAC expectations may fail with a /80 prefix
network.explanation: Many IPv6 SLAAC implementations depend on a /64 prefix for generating ordinary addresses. Changing the LAN to /80 can break that behavior; it does not imply NAT66, stop TCP, or remove the general need for router advertisements.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A host has IPv6 address fe80::abcd on one interface. Which is true about communication to another router across multiple routed networks?
options: The address is link-local and is not forwarded by routers
The address identifies all IPv6 nodes
The address is a DNS-specific address
network.explanation: fe80::/10 addresses are link-local and not routed across links. They can be used for same-link next-hop communication.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: An IPv6 engineer needs a stable link-local next-hop for a static route. Which address type should be used with the correct egress interface?
network.explanation: IPv6 can route to a link-local next hop on a specified interface. Multicast, loopback, and IPv4 broadcast are not appropriate unicast next hops.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A host must reach an IPv4-only application while itself being on an IPv6-only network. Which architecture can translate the protocol families?
network.explanation: NAT64 translates between IPv6 and IPv4, often paired with DNS64. SLAAC, ARP, and VLAN tagging cannot perform protocol-family translation.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A team captures IPv6 traffic and sees requests to ff02::1. Which statement BEST describes that destination?
options: It is a globally routable unicast server
It identifies a single DNS resolver
It is an IPv6 loopback destination
It is the link-local all-nodes multicast group
network.explanation: ff02::1 targets all IPv6 nodes on the local link. It is not unicast, loopback, or globally routable.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: An office AP reports 2.4 GHz congestion and overlapping co-channel interference. Nearby APs use channels 1, 6, and 11 with 20 MHz widths. Which change is MOST likely to improve capacity without increasing interference?
options: Enable 2.4 GHz 40 MHz channels on every AP
Increase all AP transmit power to maximum
Prefer 5 GHz and tune the channel and transmit-power plan
Disable wireless security to improve throughput
network.explanation: Client steering to 5 GHz and coordinated channel/power planning can improve airtime efficiency. Wider 2.4 GHz channels and excess power can worsen congestion.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: Wireless clients have strong RSSI but poor throughput; an analyzer shows heavy competing traffic on the same channel. What is MOST likely wrong?
options: The channel has high airtime utilization and contention
The DHCP pool is too large
The trunk has jumbo frames enabled
network.explanation: Strong signal does not ensure free airtime. Co-channel contention can reduce throughput even at excellent RSSI.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A PoE+ access point reboots whenever all radios transmit at full power. Switch logs show the PoE budget exceeded. What is the BEST remediation?
options: Provide a suitable PoE power budget or compatible injector
network.explanation: The device needs sufficient PoE power. DHCP, mirroring and radio power increases do not fix inadequate electrical power.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A 10 Gb fiber link stays down after replacing a transceiver. Fiber is seated, but the switch reports unsupported optics. Which FIRST action is justified?
options: Verify transceiver speed, fiber standard, and vendor compatibility
network.explanation: Unsupported or incompatible optics can prevent link negotiation. VLANs, STP, and IP settings cannot fix unsupported transceiver hardware.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A 100-meter copper link has intermittent CRC errors after a bundle of cables was routed beside high-voltage wiring. Which explanation BEST fits?
network.explanation: Copper Ethernet can suffer EMI and physical-layer degradation. DNS, OSPF and recovery planning do not cause CRC errors.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: An organization wants two 1 GbE switch ports to act as a single logical link with load distribution and link redundancy. Which protocol is MOST suitable?
network.explanation: LACP negotiates an aggregated logical link. STP prevents loops, LLDP discovers neighbors, and 802.1X authenticates ports.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A Linux hypervisor has 192.168.1.35/28 on vmbr0. The switch port is native VLAN 3, whose gateway is 192.168.1.65/26. The hypervisor cannot ping the gateway. Which correction is BEST?
options: Use an IP and mask from 192.168.1.64/26, with appropriate gateway
network.explanation: 192.168.1.35/28 belongs to 192.168.1.32/28 while the stated VLAN 3 gateway is in 192.168.1.64/26. Fix the host addressing; the cable, PoE and DNS are not the mismatch.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A Windows workstation shows valid DHCP IP, subnet mask, default gateway and DNS. It can ping an external IP but cannot resolve an internal hostname. Which test is BEST next?
options: nslookup for the internal name against the configured DNS server
Change the native VLAN without checking it
network.explanation: The failure isolates to internal name resolution. Testing the configured DNS server with nslookup is appropriate before disruptive changes.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: After a routing change, packets to one branch take a longer path. Traceroute shows an unexpected next hop, while local reachability and DNS still work. What should you inspect FIRST?
options: Routing table and route advertisement priorities
network.explanation: Traceroute points to a routing path issue, so inspect route selection and metrics. DHCP/DNS and PoE do not explain an unexpected routed hop.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A workstation can ping its subnet gateway, but cannot access a remote application on TCP 443. Ping to the remote server works. What is MOST useful next?
options: Test TCP 443 connectivity and firewall/security policies
network.explanation: ICMP reachability does not establish that TCP 443 is permitted or listening. A port-specific connection test and policy inspection are warranted.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A switch interface shows up/up and many input CRC errors. Users experience intermittent drops. Which investigative step BEST narrows the cause?
options: Test the physical link, cable, terminations and optics
network.explanation: CRC counters suggest corrupted frames in the physical/link path; systematic link testing is higher value than application or DNS changes.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A wireless SSID assigned to tagged VLAN 20 is visible, but clients never receive DHCP addresses. The AP is online using native VLAN 10. What should be verified FIRST?
options: Tagged VLAN 20 is permitted end-to-end on the AP uplink to the DHCP path
SSID broadcast name matches the DHCP hostname
All clients have static public IPs
The 5 GHz signal is stronger than 2.4 GHz

network.question: A service team wants a virtual firewall appliance instead of a dedicated physical firewall while preserving similar packet inspection functions. What model BEST describes the change?
network.explanation: NFV implements network functions as software instances instead of fixed-function hardware. The alternatives address links, DNS, or storage.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A global service must direct clients to nearby healthy service endpoints using DNS responses. Which technology BEST fits?
network.explanation: DNS-based routing policies can return healthy nearby service endpoints. ARP and DHCP are local network functions.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A business migrates from managing operating systems on virtual machines to deploying application code on a provider-managed runtime. Which change is occurring?
network.explanation: PaaS moves much of runtime and OS administration to the provider, unlike IaaS. The alternatives do not describe that responsibility change.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A network analyst captures packets showing repeated TCP SYNs but no SYN-ACKs from a service. Which problem category BEST matches the evidence?
options: ARP resolution failure on every host
network.explanation: Without SYN-ACK, TCP handshake does not complete. TLS occurs later; ARP might be a separate cause but is not proven.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A provider advertises autoscaling during traffic spikes and removal of extra capacity after demand falls. Which cloud property is MOST directly demonstrated?
network.explanation: Elasticity adjusts capacity with demand. Colocation, static routing and cold-site planning are separate concepts.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A cloud provider hosts multiple organizations on shared infrastructure while logically isolating their workloads. Which model is MOST relevant?

network.question: An enterprise needs to connect AWS and an on-premises network without relying on the public internet as the primary data path. Which option BEST fits?

network.explanation: Dedicated private cloud connectivity addresses private WAN integration. NAT and DNS do not create dedicated links.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A switch receives frames from an endpoint on an access port in VLAN 25. How does it normally forward them over a trunk that allows VLAN 25?

As broadcast ARP requests regardless of destination
As new IP packets with a changed gateway
network.explanation: Access frames are classified into VLAN 25 and sent tagged across an 802.1Q trunk unless it is the trunk native VLAN.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: After adding a redundant inter-switch link, MAC flapping appears between two ports. Which diagnosis is MOST plausible?
network.explanation: MAC addresses alternately learned on redundant paths suggest a Layer 2 loop. STP and loop control should be reviewed.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A PC should remain in VLAN 12 untagged, but a connected VoIP phone needs VLAN 22 tagged through the same switch port. What configuration BEST supports both?
options: Access VLAN 22 only with tags blocked
Native VLAN 22 with no other tags
network.explanation: Untagged PC traffic can use VLAN 12 while phone voice traffic is tagged VLAN 22. A single access VLAN alone cannot carry both populations.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: An engineer needs to ensure only approved DHCP server replies can enter a campus access network. Which ports should be trusted for DHCP snooping?
options: Only verified paths toward authorized DHCP servers
All ports that connect to printers
network.explanation: Trust only authorized DHCP-server-facing paths. Trusting edge ports defeats rogue DHCP protection.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A switch has a native VLAN mismatch with its neighbor; both allow VLAN 100 and 200 tagged. What is the BEST operational concern?
options: Untagged management or control traffic may be classified into the wrong VLAN
Tagged VLANs automatically become public IP networks
Link negotiation always drops to 10 Mbps
The switches both disable IPv6 routing
network.explanation: A native VLAN mismatch reclassifies untagged frames and may leak or disrupt management traffic. It does not necessarily break physical link or all tagged VLANs.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A trunk is configured to permit VLANs 10 and 20, but not VLAN 30. An AP sends guest traffic tagged VLAN 30. What is the MOST likely outcome?
options: VLAN 30 traffic is blocked on that trunk
The AP converts the guest SSID to IPv6 only
VLAN 30 traffic bypasses the switch DHCP policy
network.explanation: A VLAN outside the trunk allowed set is not forwarded. It is not silently reclassified to VLAN 10.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide

network.question: A network requires a switch to block redundant links temporarily while still retaining failover. Which technology is most directly responsible?
network.explanation: RSTP selects forwarding and alternate links to prevent loops while enabling quicker convergence. VRRP is gateway redundancy, not Layer 2 loop control.
network.source: Network+ N10-009 · Scenario-based practice inspired by the uploaded guide
